title: NHRC, India takessuo motucognizance of the reported death of one person and injuries to another after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole at a factory in Faridabad district, Haryana
subtitle:
Issues a notice to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Faridabad Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report expected to include the status of the investigation of the case, health of the injured as well as compensation, if any, provided to him and the NoK of the deceased
body_text:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that on 11th August 2026, one person died and another got injured after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole at a factory in Sector-25 of Faridabad district, Haryana. Reportedly, they descended into the manhole without any safety equipment.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Faridabad Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation, health of the injured, as well as compensation, if any, provided to him and the NoK of the deceased.
According to the media report, carried on 11th August 2026, the workers were called by the factory owner to clean the manhole.
***
NSK

enrichment.summary: The NHRC took suo motu cognizance of a media report that on 11 August 2026, one person died and another was injured after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole without safety equipment at a factory in Sector-25, Faridabad, Haryana. The Commission issued notices to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Faridabad Police Commissioner seeking a detailed report within two weeks, covering the investigation status, the injured worker's health, and compensation provided to him and the deceased's next of kin.
enrichment.context:
Manual scavenging and hazardous manhole/sewer cleaning deaths remain a persistent issue in India despite the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, which bans manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks without protective gear and mandates mechanized cleaning. The Supreme Court, in Safai Karamchari Andolan vs Union of India (2014) and subsequent orders, directed compensation of Rs 10 lakh to families of those who die during sewer/septic tank cleaning. Despite this legal framework, deaths from asphyxiation due to toxic gases (like hydrogen sulphide and methane) in manholes continue to be reported frequently across states, often involving contractual or informal workers hired without safety equipment, training, or oversight—highlighting weak enforcement of both labour safety and manual scavenging laws.

The NHRC's suo motu action is a recurring pattern seen in similar manhole/sewer death cases nationwide, where it invokes Article 21 (right to life) and directs state authorities to report on FIR registration, accountability of employers, and compensation disbursal. Such interventions serve as an accountability mechanism, but recurring incidents indicate that ground-level enforcement of sanitation worker safety norms remains inadequate, an issue of significance for governance and social justice discourse.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is correct?
options: It can take suo motu cognizance of human rights violations and issue notices to authorities for reports.
Its recommendations are legally binding on state governments.
It has the power to award compensation directly and enforce recovery from violators.
It was established under a constitutional amendment.
prelims_questions.explanation: The NHRC, a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, can take suo motu cognizance of human rights violations and issue notices seeking reports, as seen in this case, but its recommendations are not legally binding and it cannot directly enforce compensation recovery.

prelims_questions.question: The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 primarily seeks to:
options: Provide reservation in government jobs for sanitation workers
Ban manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks without protective equipment and provide for rehabilitation of manual scavengers
Regulate wages of factory workers in hazardous industries
Establish a national compensation fund for industrial accidents
prelims_questions.explanation: The 2013 Act prohibits manual scavenging and hazardous manual cleaning of sewers/septic tanks without safety gear, and provides for identification and rehabilitation of manual scavengers.

mains_questions.question: Despite legal safeguards, deaths due to manual cleaning of sewers and manholes continue to occur in India. Discuss the reasons for poor implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013, and suggest measures to ensure worker safety.

Examine the role of the National Human Rights Commission in safeguarding the rights of vulnerable and informal sector workers. What are the limitations of its suo motu powers in ensuring accountability?
